title: No Erasing!
sub: Grades 1–2 · The typewriter and the computer
objective: Children will compare the two machines in the exhibition’s display case, a typewriter and a computer, and find out what each does with a mistake. They will hear the story of writing tools, from scribes to the internet, and learn the exhibition’s big idea: each new tool let more people write and share their words.

objectives.heading: By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
objectives.why: Long ago, only a few people could write. Every new writing tool opened the door a little wider, and now it is open to you.

items.question: say what happens to a mistake on each machine?

connection: **Visit the exhibition:** the display case holds the typewriter and the iMac side by side. At the Typing Station, *Race the machines*: type the same line on both.

steps.title: Oops!
script: Open the Typing Station. On its typewriter, type *CAT* but make a mistake: *CAR*. Press Back space and type *T*: the T lands right on top of the R. Ask: *“Where did the mistake go?”* It is still there! On a typewriter there is no erasing; you can only strike over. Now do the same on the iMac tab: Back space takes the mistake away. *“Today we find out why people were so excited about machines for writing.”*

steps.title: Who could write?
script: Play the four sounds in order and tell the story on page 3 as you go. *A quill pen:* for thousands of years, only a few people could write. *A printing press:* around 1440, books began to cost much less, and many more people learned to read. *A typewriter:* from 1868, ordinary people could make neat papers, and many women went to work as typists, earning their own money. *A computer keyboard:* now anyone can fix their writing, and share it with the world.

steps.title: Typewriter rules
script: Give every child a pen and a strip of paper. *“Typewriter rules: pen only, no erasing. If you make a mistake, write right over it, like a strike-over.”* Children copy the line from the screen: *Now everyone can write.* Then ask: *“How did it feel, writing when you couldn’t erase?”*
steps.purpose: Feel what a typist felt: every letter counts, and a mistake stays.
students: No erasing! A mistake? Write right over it.

steps.title: Choose a handout
script: Children choose a handout. All three compare the typewriter and the computer, and put the four ways of writing in order.

levels.name: Green Level
levels.summary: Circle *typewriter* or *computer* for four sentences, number four picture-clue cards in story order, copy a line by typewriter rules and draw their favorite writing tool.

levels.name: Yellow Level
levels.summary: Sort six sentences, order the four tools by their dates, copy the Typing Station’s own line by typewriter rules, then say which machine they like better, and why.

levels.name: Red Level
levels.summary: Write their own chart of the two machines, order the tools and say who could write with each, then write a note by typewriter rules and plan what they would share with the world.

steps.purpose: Sort, order and write at the right level of challenge.
students: Choose Green, Yellow or Red. All three compare the typewriter and the computer, and put the tools in order.

steps.title: Look back
script: Ask the objectives back as questions, from the screen or page 1: *“Can you now…?”* Children show a thumb up, sideways or down. Ask one child to answer each aloud.

steps.title: Which did you like better?
script: Then ask the Typing Station’s own question: *“On the typewriter, a mistake stays on the page. On the computer, Back space takes it away. Which did you like better? Why?”*
